::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this page is for

Use this page to check how a classified CVD death is linked to a hospital event,
and how deaths that cannot be linked uniquely contribute to aggregate event
estimates. The process has two broad procedures:

1. **Link individual records.** The workflow tries to connect each classified
   CVD death to one person in the hospital-event data. When it finds one unique
   person, it checks whether a Heart or Stroke event occurred during the 0–27
   days before death.

2. **Estimate the remaining contribution in aggregate**. A death remains unresolved when the workflow cannot match it reliably to exactly one person in the hospital-event data. This includes deaths with no acceptable person match, more than one possible match, or contradictory identity information. It is different from a directly identified additional DCO: where one person is matched but that person has no qualifying Heart or Stroke event in the 0–27 days before death, the workflow classifies the death directly as an additional DCO. The unresolved group may contain both additional DCOs and deaths whose hospital event could not be linked reliably. The workflow therefore estimates their contribution only within group totals; it never assigns an estimated outcome to an individual death.

The associated CVD event workflow is [Step 4: Generate combined CVD metrics](../workflows/cvd-events/generate-metrics.qmd).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Rules at a glance

**Procedure 1 — link individual records**

- Try the ordered person-linkage rules **L01**, **L02** and **L03**.
- Accept a match only when exactly one eligible CVD person is found.
- For a matched person, treat a Heart or Stroke event **0–27 days before death**
  as an already-recorded episode.
- Treat a matched death with no event in that window as an additional DCO.
- Leave a death unresolved when one person cannot be identified uniquely.

**Procedure 2 — estimate unresolved deaths in aggregate**

- Use the resolved deaths to estimate what proportion of unresolved deaths are
  likely to represent additional DCOs.
- Apply that proportion only to group totals. Never assign an estimated result
  to an individual record.
:::

## Scope and candidate pools

This table defines which death and hospital-event records enter the linkage
process and which information must remain private.

| Rule | Implemented requirement |
|---|---|
| Mortality pool | Run linkage once against deaths in the **Inclusive** BNR-Heart-or-Stroke definition with a valid death date no later than the selected CVD event-data coverage end. Retain the Primary and Inclusive flags from that same linkage run. |
| Event pool | Use hospital-recorded Heart and Stroke events (`dco == 0`) with valid event date and event type within the selected CVD coverage. Exclude legacy imported DCO rows (`dco == 1`) from the new linkage pool. |
| Definition relationship | Primary is a subset of Inclusive. They are alternative mortality definitions, not lower and upper linkage confidence limits. |
| Confidentiality | All person identifiers, possible matches, linkage reasons, episode dates and component evidence remain private. Only approved aggregate results may enter a public data package release. |

## Identity preparation rules

Before any records are compared, the workflow standardises the identifiers used
for matching and rejects identity information that is ambiguous or contradictory.

| Field | Implemented rule |
|---|---|
| National Registration Number (NRN) | Keep as text so leading zeroes are preserved. Remove spaces and hyphens. Require exactly 10 digits and a valid `YYMMDD` date prefix. |
| NRN century | Resolve 1900/2000 only when one date is compatible with explicit CVD date of birth, or with age and event/death date within one year. An ambiguous NRN-derived date is not sufficient. |
| Sex | CVD source `1 = female`, `2 = male`. Mortality source text `"1" = male`, `"2" = female`. Compare the canonical values. |
| Names | Convert to upper case, trim repeated spaces and replace `. , - / ( )` and apostrophes with token boundaries. Do not use fuzzy, phonetic or partial-string similarity. |
| Boundary names | For L03, compare the first and last normalised tokens in either order. |
| Contradictory CVD identity | A valid NRN group with conflicting non-missing sex or explicit dates of birth is not rescued by a name match. |

## Ordered person-linkage rules

This table shows how the workflow tries to identify one person, starting with
the strongest identifier and moving to names, sex and date or age only when the
earlier rule does not produce a match. A person accepted by an earlier rule is
not reconsidered by a later rule.

| Rule | Match requirement |
|---|---|
| **L01 — exact NRN** | One valid, unique death NRN has a valid CVD counterpart; the CVD NRN group has no conflicting sex or date of birth; and mortality sex and NRN-derived date of birth do not contradict the CVD identity. |
| **L02 — full name, sex and date of birth** | L01 did not match because the mortality NRN is invalid or there is no valid CVD NRN counterpart; the normalised full name, canonical sex and exact resolved date of birth match; and exactly one CVD person proxy remains. Repeated events for that same person count as one candidate. |
| **L03 — boundary names, sex and date/age** | L02 did not produce one match; first and surname boundary tokens match in either order; canonical sex matches; and either the resolved dates of birth match exactly or one date of birth is absent and the years-only age at death agrees within one year. Exactly one CVD person proxy must remain. |

### Matches that are not accepted

This table lists the circumstances in which a possible match must remain
unresolved rather than being selected automatically.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| More than one eligible person | Leave unresolved; do not choose between candidates. |
| Conflicting non-missing NRNs, sex values or explicit dates of birth | Leave unresolved; a shared name or date does not override the contradiction. |
| Different known dates of birth | Do not use age to rescue the match. |
| Age not explicitly recorded in years | Do not use the L03 age fallback. |
| Approximate or fuzzy name similarity | No match. |

## Episode and DCO rules

After the linkage rules have been tried, this table shows how a unique person
match and the timing of any qualifying event determine whether the death is
already represented, is an additional DCO or remains unresolved.

| Rule | Implemented result |
|---|---|
| Person matched; qualifying event 0–27 days before death | `recorded_event_0_27_days`: the fatal episode is already represented in hospital event data. Day 0 and day 27 are included. |
| Person matched; no qualifying event 0–27 days before death | `provisional_additional_dco`: deterministic additional DCO. |
| Nearest qualifying event more than 27 days before death | Retain as a private remote-event diagnostic. It does not prevent provisional additional-DCO status. |
| No unique person match | Unresolved candidate. Do not label the person as a DCO. |
| Future event after death | Not a prior fatal episode. |

## Aggregate unresolved-DCO estimation

After individual linkage is complete, this table shows how the workflow uses
resolved deaths to estimate the additional DCO contribution from unresolved
deaths for each mortality definition and death year.

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Resolved fraction | Let `L` be resolved deaths with a recorded 0–27-day episode and `A` be deterministic additional DCOs. Calculate `p = A / (L + A)`. |
| Minimum evidence | Use the target year's `p` only when `L + A >= 20`. Otherwise use the same definition pooled over target year ±1; if still below 20, use all available years. If the all-years pool is below 20, produce no central estimate. |
| Unresolved application | Apply `p` to the aggregate unresolved count `U`. Do not apply it to individual records. |
| Lower component | `A`. |
| Central component | `A + (p × U)`. This may be fractional. |
| Upper component | `A + U`. |
| Definition check | For the same annual stratum, the Inclusive All-CVD lower, central and upper components must not be below the corresponding Primary components. |

## Heart, Stroke and mixed allocation

Once the All-CVD aggregate has been estimated, this table shows how the total is
divided between Heart, Stroke and cases that cannot be assigned to one family.

| Rule | Implemented requirement |
|---|---|
| Heart | Certificate and linked episode evidence follow the Heart attribution routes. |
| Stroke | Certificate and linked episode evidence follow the Stroke attribution routes. |
| Mixed/unallocated | Both families, discordant certificate and episode families, unclassified evidence and unresolved attribution remain in a separate private category. They are not forced into Heart or Stroke. |
| Common allocation source | Use the observed deterministic additional-DCO composition from the same annual, three-year or all-years resolved pool selected for the target year. |
| Joint allocation | Allocate the All-CVD unresolved central and upper components across Heart, Stroke and mixed/unallocated using `selected category A / selected total A`. |
| Accounting check | Heart + Stroke + mixed/unallocated must equal All CVD at the lower, central and upper bounds. |
| Independent subtype estimate | May be retained as private sensitivity evidence, but the joint allocation is the production result. |

## Public aggregation boundaries

- DCO enhancement starts with complete calendar year 2010; 2008–2009 are not included.
- Deaths without usable age remain in counts but are excluded from direct age standardisation.
- Hospital-only + additional DCO must equal hospital-plus-DCO for every matching annual stratum.

## Where the rules are implemented

The monthly controller is `scripts/stata/monthly/bnr_step4_metrics.do`. There is no single linkage-rules file: the ordered rules are implemented in these `.do` files.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Linkage and estimation code

This table identifies the maintained Stata files that implement each part of
the individual-linkage and aggregate-estimation process.

| File | Rule set |
|---|---|
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_prepare_linkage_inputs.do` | Builds the Inclusive death pool and hospital-event pool and applies coverage limits. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_l01_episode_core.do` | Applies L01 and the 0–27-day episode rule. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_l02_l03_episode_core.do` | Applies L02 and L03, then repeats the episode rule for all accepted matches. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_estimate_unresolved_core.do` | Applies the aggregate unresolved-DCO fraction and fallback hierarchy. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_profile_subtype_concordance_core.do` | Creates Heart/Stroke certificate-versus-episode attribution routes. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_estimate_joint_subtype_core.do` | Applies the production Heart/Stroke/mixed joint allocation. |
| `scripts/stata/metrics/cvd/bnr_cvd_construct_incidence_rates_core.do` | Carries the aggregate DCO components into annual counts and rates. |
:::

## Change rule

Do not change these rules during a routine data release. For an agreed change,
update the controlling contract, code, tests and this page together.
